chunks: In both of them there will be every kind of fruits in pairs.

key_terms.فِيهِمَا: In both of them (referring to the two gardens of Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the fruits in Paradise?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the phrase 'every fruit in pairs' (kulli fākihatin zawājin) is often interpreted not merely as literal botanical pairing but as a symbol of perfect harmony, completeness, and the absence of deficiency in the eternal abode. This verse reinforces the concept of divine generosity (karām) in Surah Ar-Rahman, where the repetition of 'Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?' underscores the infinite nature of these blessings. The 'two gardens' refer to the two distinct realms of bliss described in the preceding verses, emphasizing the structured and abundant nature of Paradise.
